prompt.hi: Kitaab mein ek darwaze ki photo tirchi chhapi hai. Kya photo wale darwaze ke kone right angle hain?
prompt.en: A photo of a door is printed slanting in a book. Are the corners of the door in the photo right angles?

hindi.hi: Kitaab mein darwaze ki photo tedhi chhapi hai. Photo wale darwaze ke kone samkon hain kya?
hindi.en: In a book the photo of a door is printed crooked. Are the corners of the door in the photo right angles?

reask.hi: Kya kitaab mein tirchi chhapi darwaze ki photo mein darwaze ke kone right angle hain?
reask.en: In a door's photo printed slanting in a book, are the door's corners right angles?

viewCaption.hi: Board par pehle asli darwaza seedha khada hai, aur phir photo wala darwaza tircha chhapa hai.
viewCaption.en: The board shows the real door standing straight first, and then the door in the photo printed slanting.

why.hi: photo mein wahi darwaza sirf tircha chhapa hai, aur tircha hone se kone nahi badalte, toh uske kone right angle hain
why.en: the photo shows the same door, only printed slanting, and slanting does not change corners, so its corners are right angles

whyShort.hi: tircha chhapne se darwaze ke kone nahi badle
whyShort.en: printing it slanting did not change the door's corners

whyAlt.hi: kitaab ko thoda ghuma do toh photo wala darwaza seedha dikhne lagta hai, aur uske kone asli darwaze jaise hi hain
whyAlt.en: turn the book a little and the door in the photo looks straight, with corners just like the real door's

simpler.hi: Photo wala darwaza bhi wahi darwaza hai, bas tircha chhapa hai. Socho, tircha hone se kone par kya asar hota hai.
simpler.en: The door in the photo is the same door, just printed slanting. Think what being slanting does to a corner.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab woh kone dekhenge jo tester mein fit nahi hote, jaise cake ki nok, aur unhe right angle se milayenge.
bridgeToNext.en: Next we look at corners that do not fit the tester, like the tip of a cake piece, and hold them against a right angle.

simpler.hi: Ab kone ko tester se milakar dekhenge ki woh right angle se kam hai ya zyada.
simpler.en: Next we hold corners against the tester to see whether they are less or more than a right angle.

hook.convey: a pointed slice tip and a game-map angle → compare each opening with the tester → less, equal or more than a right angle; long lines do not make an angle bigger

use.hi: Kitchen mein cake ka ek slice dekho, uski nok patli hoti hai. Aaj dekhenge ki woh nok right angle se kam khuli hai ya zyada.
use.en: Look at a slice of cake in the kitchen; its tip is narrow. Today we see whether that tip opens less or more than a right angle.

use.hi: Video game ke map mein kisi angle ki lines bahut lambi ho sakti hain. Aaj dekhenge ki lambi lines se angle bada hota hai ya nahi.
use.en: On a video game map the lines of an angle can be very long. Today we see whether long lines make an angle bigger or not.

explain.convey: tester on a corner → corner narrower than the tester = less than a right angle; exact fit = equal; corner opens wider than the tester = more than a right angle

point.hi: Pehle tester ko kone par tikao. Agar kona tester se tang hai, toh woh right angle se kam hai. Agar kona tester se zyada khula hai, toh woh right angle se zyada hai. Bilkul fit ho, toh right angle ke barabar.
point.en: First set the tester against the corner. If the corner is narrower than the tester, it is less than a right angle. If the corner opens wider than the tester, it is more than a right angle. If it fits exactly, it equals a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ek kitaab khuli rakhi hai. Tester ko panno ke kone mein rakha, toh ek panna tester ke bahar nikal gaya. Yeh angle right angle se kam hai ya zyada?
prompt.en: A book lies open. When the tester is put in the corner between its pages, one page goes outside the tester. Is this angle less or more than a right angle?

why.hi: ek panna tester ke bahar nikla, yaani kona tester se zyada khula hai, aur tester khud ek right angle hai
why.en: one page went outside the tester, so the corner opens wider than the tester, and the tester itself is a right angle

simpler.hi: Tester ko kone se milao. Kona tester se tang ho toh angle chhota hai, aur tester se bhi khula ho toh angle bada hai.
simpler.en: Hold the tester against the corner. If the corner is narrower than the tester the angle is smaller, and if it opens beyond the tester the angle is bigger.

explain.convey: angle P: square corner with short arms; angle Q: square corner with long arms → the tester fits both → same angle; an angle is how wide the arms open, not how long they are

point.hi: Angle bhuja ki lambai se nahi, uske khulne se naapte hain. Bhuja chhoti ho ya lambi, agar tester bilkul fit hota hai, toh woh square corner hai. Yeh khulna hi angle hai.
point.en: An angle is measured by how wide it opens, not by the length of its arms. Short arms or long, if the tester fits exactly, it is a square corner. This opening is the angle.

prompt.hi: Ek kone ki bhuja 3 cm hai, doosre ki 12 cm, aur dono par tester bilkul fit hota hai. Kaunsa angle bada hai, ya dono barabar?
prompt.en: One corner has arms 3 cm long, another has arms 12 cm long, and the tester fits both exactly. Which angle is bigger, or are both equal?

why.hi: tester dono par bilkul fit hota hai, aur 3 cm ya 12 cm ki bhuja khulna nahi badalti
why.en: the tester fits both exactly, and arms of 3 cm or 12 cm do not change the opening

simpler.hi: Bhuja lambi ho ya chhoti, angle usse nahi badalta. Sirf dekho ki kona kitna khula hai.
simpler.en: Long arms or short arms, that does not change the angle. Just look at how wide the corner opens.

explain.convey: an angle changes with its opening, not its arm length → long scissors opened a little: to make the angle bigger, open them wider, not make the blades longer

point.hi: Angle bhuja ki lambai se nahi, khulne se badalta hai. Bhuja lambi ho par thoda sa khula ho, toh angle chhota hi rehta hai. Jo zyada khula hai, wahi bada angle hai.
point.en: An angle changes with its opening, not its arm length. Long arms opened a little still make a small angle. The one that opens wider is the bigger angle.

prompt.hi: Ek lambi kainchi thodi si khuli hai, aur tumhe uska angle bada karna hai. Kya karoge: blade aur lambi karoge, ya kainchi aur khologe?
prompt.en: A long pair of scissors is opened slightly, and you want to make its angle bigger. What will you do: make the blades longer, or open the scissors wider?

why.hi: angle kainchi ka khulna hai; blade aur lambi karoge toh khulna wahi rahega, kainchi aur khologe tabhi angle bada hoga
why.en: the angle is the opening; longer blades keep the same opening, and only opening the scissors wider makes it bigger

simpler.hi: Yaad rakho, angle blade ki lambai nahi hai. Angle do blades ke beech ka khulna hai.
simpler.en: Remember, the angle is not the length of the blades. The angle is the opening between the two blades.

problem.hi: Rani ki rangoli mein 3 kone hain. Kone P ki bhuja 9 cm hai, aur woh tester ke andar reh jaata hai, beech mein khaali jagah. Kone Q ki bhuja 4 cm hai, aur tester bilkul fit hota hai. Kone R ki bhuja 3 cm hai, aur uski ek bhuja tester ke bahar jaati hai. Sabse bada angle kaunsa hai?
problem.en: Rani's rangoli has 3 corners. Corner P has arms 9 cm long and stays inside the tester, with empty space between. Corner Q has arms 4 cm long and the tester fits exactly. Corner R has arms 3 cm long and one arm goes outside the tester. Which is the biggest angle?

simpler.hi: Teen kone P, Q aur R hain. Tester se dekhkar batana hai ki inmein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai.
simpler.en: There are three corners, P, Q and R. Using the tester, we say which of them is the biggest angle.

givens.hi: Teeno kone tester se mile: P mein khaali jagah bachi, Q bilkul fit hua, aur R tester ke bahar gaya.
givens.en: All three corners met the tester: P left empty space, Q fit exactly, and R went outside the tester.

find.hi: teeno mein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai
find.en: which of the three is the biggest angle

do.hi: P aur Q ko tester se milao
do.en: Compare P and Q with the tester

steps.result: P right angle se kam, Q right angle ke barabar

why.hi: P tester se tang hai aur Q bilkul fit hota hai
why.en: P is narrower than the tester and Q fits exactly

simpler.hi: P tester se tang hai, toh P right angle se chhota hai. Q tester mein bilkul fit hai, toh Q right angle hai.
simpler.en: P is narrower than the tester, so P is smaller than a right angle. Q fits the tester exactly, so Q is a right angle.

do.hi: Ab R ko tester se milao
do.en: Now compare R with the tester

why.hi: R ki ek bhuja tester ke bahar jaati hai, yaani R zyada khula hai
why.en: one arm of R goes outside the tester, so R opens wider

simpler.hi: R ki ek bhuja tester se bahar nikalti hai. Matlab R tester se bhi zyada khula hai, right angle se bada.
simpler.en: One arm of R goes outside the tester. That means R opens even wider than the tester, more than a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ab bhuja ki lambai chhodo, sirf khulna dekho. Teeno mein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai?
prompt.en: Now ignore the arm lengths and look only at the opening. Which of the three is the biggest angle?

simpler.hi: Bhuja ki lambai mat dekho. Jo kona tester se bhi zyada khula hai, wahi sabse bada angle hai.
simpler.en: Do not look at the arm lengths. The corner that opens even wider than the tester is the biggest angle.

why.hi: P mein khaali jagah bachi, Q bilkul fit hua, par R tester ke bahar jaata hai, toh R sabse khula hai
why.en: P left empty space and Q fit exactly, but R's arm goes outside the tester, so R opens the most

answer.hi: teeno mein sabse bada angle R hai
answer.en: R is the biggest of the three angles

why.hi: R sabse zyada khula hai, aur P ki lambi bhuja se uska angle bada nahi hota
why.en: R opens the widest, and P's long arms do not make its angle bigger

prompt.hi: {friend} ne ek angle ki bhuja 15 cm se 30 cm kar di, aur khulna wahi rakha. Ab angle pehle se bada hai, chhota hai, ya utna hi?
prompt.en: {friend} made an angle's arms 30 cm instead of 15 cm, and kept the opening the same. Is the angle now bigger, smaller, or the same as before?

why.hi: angle khulna hai, aur khulna wahi raha jo pehle tha; bhuja 15 cm se 30 cm karne se angle nahi badalta
why.en: the angle is the opening, which stayed as before; 30 cm arms instead of 15 cm do not change it

simpler.hi: Angle bhuja ki lambai nahi, uska khulna hai. Socho, yahan khulna badla ya nahi.
simpler.en: An angle is its opening, not its arm length. Think whether the opening changed here.

prompt.hi: Ek darwaze ke kone ki ek bhuja 2 m lambi hai, aur tester us kone par bilkul fit hota hai. {friend} ka kehna hai ki yeh angle right angle se bada hai, kyunki bhuja bahut lambi hai. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: A door's corner has one arm 2 m long, and the tester fits that corner exactly. {friend} says this angle is bigger than a right angle because the arm is very long. Is that right?

accept: nahi, right angle ke barabar hai
no, it equals a right angle

why.hi: tester bilkul fit hota hai, toh angle right angle ke barabar hai; 2 m lambi bhuja khulna nahi badalti
why.en: the tester fits exactly, so the angle equals a right angle; 2 m long arms do not change the opening

simpler.hi: Bhuja ki lambai chhodo, sirf tester dekho. Yaad karo, tester bilkul fit ho toh angle kitna hota hai.
simpler.en: Forget the arm length and look only at the tester. Remember what an angle is when the tester fits exactly.

prompt.hi: Ek angle ki bhuja 20 cm lambi hai, par woh kona tester se tang hai. Right angle ke mukable yeh angle kam hai ya zyada?
prompt.en: An angle has arms 20 cm long, but the corner is narrower than the tester. Compared with a right angle, is this angle less or more?

why.hi: kona tester se tang hai, aur 20 cm lambi bhuja use zyada nahi kholti
why.en: the corner is narrower than the tester, and 20 cm arms do not open it any wider

simpler.hi: Bhuja kitni bhi lambi ho, angle sirf khulne se naapte hain. Ab socho, tester se tang kona right angle se chhota hai ya bada.
simpler.en: However long the arms are, an angle is measured only by its opening. Now think whether a corner narrower than the tester is smaller or bigger than a right angle.

ladder.why: a pizza tip narrower than a napkin corner → less than a right angle
long arms opened a little vs a short square corner → the square corner is bigger
say why longer arms do not make a bigger angle → an angle is the opening

remediation.move: two-arm angle maker: hold the opening fixed, stretch the arms longer and longer → the opening does not change → then lay the paper tester on it

say.hi: Angle ka khulna pakad lo aur bhuja chhoti se lambi karte jao. Khulna wahi rehta hai, toh angle bhi wahi rehta hai.
say.en: Hold the angle's opening still and make its arms longer and longer. The opening stays the same, so the angle stays the same too.

simpler.hi: Bhuja lambi karo, khulna wahi rehta hai. Toh angle bhi wahi rehta hai.
simpler.en: Make the arms longer and the opening stays the same. So the angle stays the same.

prompt.hi: 4 cm blade wali kainchi tester se zyada khuli, 16 cm wali tang. {friend} ka kehna hai: 4 cm wali ka angle bada. Sahi?
prompt.en: 4 cm-blade scissors open wider than the tester, 16 cm ones narrower. {friend} says the 4 cm angle is bigger. Right?

accept: haan, 4 cm wali ka angle bada hai

why.hi: 4 cm blade wali tester se zyada khuli, 16 cm wali tang; toh 4 cm wali ka angle bada
why.en: the 4 cm blades open wider than the tester, the 16 cm blades narrower; so the 4 cm angle is bigger

simpler.hi: Blade ki lambai mat dekho. Sirf yeh dekho ki tester ke mukable kaun kitni khuli hai.
simpler.en: Do not look at the blade length. Just see how far each pair opens compared with the tester.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak hum kone aur angle dekh rahe the. Ab ek aisi shape dekhenge jismein koi kona hi nahi hota: circle.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we looked at corners and angles. Next we look at a shape that has no corner at all: the circle.

simpler.hi: Kone aur angle hum dekh chuke. Agle hisse mein ek aisi shape dekhenge jisme koi kona hota hi nahi, circle.
simpler.en: We have seen corners and angles. Next we meet a shape with no corner at all, the circle.

hook.convey: draw round a bangle, or mark a big circle in the playground with a rope and chalk → a circle has a centre, and every point on it is the same distance from the centre

use.hi: Ek chudi kaagaz par rakho aur uske kinaare par pencil ghumakar drawing banao. Jo shape banegi, woh circle hai. Aaj dekhenge ki circle ki khaas baat kya hai.
use.en: Put a bangle on paper and run a pencil round its edge to make a drawing. The shape you get is a circle. Today we see what is special about a circle.

use.hi: Playground mein ek game ke liye bada circle banana hai. Aaj seekhenge ki rassi aur chalk se sahi circle kaise banta hai.
use.en: A big circle is needed in the playground for a game. Today we learn how a rope and chalk make a true circle.

explain.convey: string compass: one end of the string held still at the centre, pencil at the other end, string kept tight → the pencil stays the string's length from the centre at every point

point.hi: String ka ek sira beech mein haath se dabakar rakho. Yeh point circle ka centre hai, Hindi mein kendra. Doosre sire par pencil baandho aur string tight rakhkar ghumao. Pencil har jagah centre se utni hi door rehti hai jitni string lambi hai.
point.en: Hold one end of the string still in the middle with your hand. This point is the circle's centre, kendra in Hindi. Tie a pencil to the other end and turn it with the string kept tight. Everywhere, the pencil stays as far from the centre as the string is long.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke kinaare ka ek point centre se 4 cm door hai. {friend} ka kehna hai ki kinaare ka koi doosra point 5 cm door hai. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: One point on this circle's edge is 4 cm from the centre. {friend} says another point on the edge is 5 cm away. Is that right?

accept: nahi, woh bhi 4 cm door hai
no, it is also 4 cm away

why.hi: string ki lambai nahi badalti, toh kinaare ka har point centre se 4 cm door hai, 5 cm nahi
why.en: the string's length does not change, so every point on the edge is 4 cm from the centre, not 5 cm

simpler.hi: String ki lambai kabhi nahi badalti. Isliye pencil har jagah centre se utni hi door rehti hai.
simpler.en: The string's length never changes. So the pencil stays the same distance from the centre everywhere.

explain.convey: coin: every point the same distance from its centre → a circle; lemon: longer one way, the distance changes → round, but not a circle

point.hi: Sikke ke kinaare ka har point centre se barabar door hai, isliye sikka circle hai. Agar kisi gol cheez mein centre se doori kahin kam, kahin zyada ho, toh woh gol toh hai, par circle nahi.
point.en: Every point on the coin's edge is equally far from its centre, so the coin is a circle. If in some round thing the distance from the centre is less in one place and more in another, it is round, but not a circle.

prompt.hi: Ek roti ke centre se kinaara ek taraf 8 cm hai aur doosri taraf 10 cm. Kya yeh roti circle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: From the centre of a roti, the edge is 8 cm away on one side and 10 cm on the other. Is this roti a circle, yes or no?

accept: no, the distances are not equal

why.hi: roti ka kinaara centre se ek taraf 8 cm aur doosri taraf 10 cm hai, toh roti circle nahi
why.en: the roti's edge is 8 cm from the centre one way, 10 cm the other, so it is not a circle

simpler.hi: Circle ki pehchaan hai: centre se kinaare ki doori har taraf ek jaisi. Doori badle, toh shape gol ho sakti hai, par circle nahi.
simpler.en: The mark of a circle: the distance from the centre to the edge is the same on every side. If the distance changes, the shape can be round, but not a circle.

explain.convey: playground circle: rope 3 m tied to a peg, chalk at the other end, rope kept tight → every chalk mark is 3 m from the peg; a mark at another distance is not on this circle

point.hi: Khoonte se 3 m ki rassi baandho, doosre sire par chalk. Rassi tight rakhkar chalo, toh chalk ka har nishaan khoonte se 3 m door aata hai. Isliye yeh sahi circle banta hai.
point.en: Tie a 3 m rope to a peg, with chalk at the other end. Walk round keeping the rope tight, and every chalk mark comes 3 m from the peg. That is why this makes a true circle.

prompt.hi: Zameen par ek nishaan khoonte se theek rassi ki lambai jitna door hai. Kya woh nishaan is circle par hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A mark on the ground is exactly one rope-length from the peg. Is that mark on this circle, yes or no?

accept: yes, it is on the circle

why.hi: is circle ka har nishaan khoonte se rassi jitna, yaani 3 m, door hai; woh nishaan bhi utna hi door hai
why.en: every mark of this circle is one rope-length, 3 m, from the peg, and that mark is just as far

simpler.hi: Rassi 3 m ki hai, toh har chalk nishaan khoonte se 3 m door aata hai. Circle par sirf wahi nishaan hain jo 3 m door hain.
simpler.en: The rope is 3 m long, so every chalk mark comes 3 m from the peg. Only marks that are 3 m away are on the circle.

problem.hi: Pooja rangoli ke liye 50 cm ki string ke ek sire par chalk baandhti hai. Doosra sira centre par pakadkar, string tight rakhkar circle banati hai. Phir ek kinaare se centre se hote hue doosre kinaare tak seedhi line kheenchti hai. Woh line kitni lambi hai?
problem.en: For a rangoli, Pooja ties chalk to one end of a 50 cm string. Holding the other end at the centre and keeping the string tight, she draws a circle. Then she draws a straight line from one edge, through the centre, to the other edge. How long is that line?

simpler.hi: Ek 50 cm ki string ka ek sira centre par hai aur doosre sire par chalk hai, aur isse circle bana. Ab ek kinaare se centre se hote hue doosre kinaare tak ki line ki lambai nikalni hai.
simpler.en: A 50 cm string has one end at the centre and chalk at the other end, and it draws a circle. Now we find the length of the line from one edge, through the centre, to the other edge.

givens.hi: 50 cm ki tight string ka ek sira centre par hai, aur line centre se hokar ek kinaare se doosre kinaare tak jaati hai.
givens.en: A tight 50 cm string has one end at the centre, and the line runs from one edge through the centre to the other edge.

find.hi: centre se hokar jaane wali line ki lambai
find.en: the length of the line through the centre

do.hi: Pehle dekho kinaara centre se kitni door hai
do.en: First see how far the edge is from the centre

steps.result: har point centre se 50 cm door

why.hi: tight string har point ko centre se 50 cm door rakhti hai
why.en: the tight string keeps every point 50 cm from the centre

simpler.hi: String tight hai aur 50 cm lambi hai. Isliye kinaare ka har point centre se 50 cm door hai.
simpler.en: The string is tight and 50 cm long. So every point on the edge is 50 cm from the centre.

do.hi: Ab line ke dono taraf dekho, centre ke is paar aur us paar
do.en: Now look at the line on both sides of the centre

steps.result: kinaare se centre tak 50 cm, centre se doosre kinaare tak 50 cm

why.hi: line centre se hokar ek kinaare se doosre kinaare tak jaati hai
why.en: the line goes through the centre from one edge to the other

simpler.hi: Line centre se hokar jaati hai. Centre ke ek taraf kinaare tak 50 cm hai, aur doosri taraf bhi 50 cm.
simpler.en: The line passes through the centre. On one side it is 50 cm to the edge, and on the other side also 50 cm.

prompt.hi: Ab dono taraf ki lambai jodo. Poori line kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: Now add the lengths on both sides. How long is the whole line?

simpler.hi: Line mein centre ke dono taraf 50 cm aata hai. Bas dono lambaiyan jodo.
simpler.en: The line has 50 cm on each side of the centre. Just add the two lengths.

why.hi: kinaare se centre tak 50 cm aur centre se doosre kinaare tak 50 cm hai, 50 + 50 = 100
why.en: edge to centre is 50 cm and centre to the other edge is 50 cm: 50 + 50 = 100

answer.en: the whole line is 100 cm long

why.hi: is line mein centre se kinaare tak ki 50 cm doori do baar aati hai, 50 + 50 = 100
why.en: the line holds the 50 cm centre-to-edge distance twice, 50 + 50 = 100

prompt.hi: Rangoli ke liye {friend} ne haath se ek gol banaya, aur Pooja ne khoonti aur tight string se. Inmein se pakka circle kiska hai?
prompt.en: For a rangoli, {friend} drew a round shape by hand, and Pooja drew one with a pin and a tight string. Whose is surely a circle?

why.hi: tight string har point ko centre se ek jitna door rakhti hai; haath se bane gol mein yeh doori badal sakti hai
why.en: a tight string keeps every point the same distance from the centre; in a hand-drawn round shape that distance can change

simpler.hi: Gol dikhna kaafi nahi hai. Socho, kiske gol mein har point centre se pakka ek jitna door rahega.
simpler.en: Looking round is not enough. Think in whose shape every point will surely stay the same distance from the centre.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne ek gol ghadi ke centre se uske kinaare tak har jagah naapa, aur har baar 7 cm aaya. {friend} ka kehna hai ki ghadi ka kinaara circle hai. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: {friend} measured from a round clock's centre to its edge all the way round, and got 7 cm every time. {friend} says the clock's edge is a circle. Is that right?

why.hi: ghadi ke kinaare ka har point centre se 7 cm door hai, jaise circle mein har point barabar door hota hai
why.en: every point of the clock's edge is 7 cm from the centre, as in a circle, where every point is equally far

simpler.hi: Har jagah naap ek hi aaya. Yaad karo, circle ke kinaare ki doori centre se kaisi hoti hai.
simpler.en: Every measurement came out the same. Remember how far a circle's edge is from its centre.

prompt.hi: Ek thali aur ek aam, dono gol dikhte hain. Inmein circle kaunsa hai: thali ya aam?
prompt.en: A plate and a mango both look round. Which of them is a circle: the plate or the mango?

why.hi: thali ke kinaare ka har point centre se barabar door hai, jabki aam ek taraf lamba hai
why.en: every point on the plate's rim is equally far from its centre, while the mango is longer one way

simpler.hi: Circle wahi hai jiska har kinaara centre se ek jitna door ho. Socho ki dono mein se kiska kinaara har taraf barabar door hai.
simpler.en: A circle is the one whose edge is the same distance from the centre everywhere. Think about which of the two has its edge equally far on every side.

ladder.why: the still point of the string → the centre
5 cm tight string → every point 5 cm from the pin
why the 2 m rope must stay tight → the same distance from the peg
harder: 6 cm string, marks at 6, 7 and 6 cm → the 7 cm mark is off the circle

remediation.move: string compass (pin, string, pencil) beside a hand-drawn oval → measure from the centre to several points on both → only one has all distances the same

say.hi: String se bane circle mein centre se har point barabar door hai. Haath se bane oval mein yeh doori badalti hai, isliye oval circle nahi.
say.en: In the circle made with a string, every point is equally far from the centre. In an oval drawn by hand this distance changes, so the oval is not a circle.

simpler.hi: Circle mein centre se har point ki doori barabar hoti hai. Oval mein yeh doori badalti hai, isliye oval circle nahi.
simpler.en: In a circle every point is the same distance from the centre. In an oval it changes, so an oval is not a circle.

prompt.hi: 12 cm ki string ghumate waqt beech mein dheeli ho gayi, aur ek gol shape bani. Kya woh circle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A 12 cm string went loose now and then while turning, and a round shape was drawn. Is it a circle, yes or no?

accept: no, it is not a circle

why.hi: dheeli string par pencil centre ke paas aayi, toh har point 12 cm door nahi raha; shape gol hai par circle nahi
why.en: a loose string let the pencil come closer, so not every point stayed 12 cm away; round, but not a circle

simpler.hi: Circle mein har point centre se string jitna door hota hai. Socho, dheeli string se yeh doori har jagah wahi rahegi kya.
simpler.en: In a circle every point is one string-length from the centre. Think whether a loose string keeps that distance the same everywhere.

prompt.hi: Ek square tile ki har bhuja 30 cm hai, aur use ghuma kar tircha rakha hai. Uske ek kone par tester rakhoge, toh kona tester se kam khula niklega, bilkul fit hoga, ya zyada khula niklega?
prompt.en: A square tile has sides of 30 cm each, and it has been turned and laid slanting. If you put the tester on one of its corners, will the corner come out less open than the tester, fit it exactly, or come out more open?

hindi.hi: Ek square tile ki har bhuja 30 cm ki hai, aur use ghuma ke tircha rakh diya hai. Uske kone par tester rakhne se kona tester se kam khulega, us mein theek baithega, ya zyada khulega?
hindi.en: A square tile has sides of 30 cm each, and it has been turned and laid slanting. If the tester is put on its corner, will the corner open less than the tester, sit in it just right, or open more?

did.hi: ghumayi hui, lambi bhuja wali square tile ka kona tester se jaancha
did.en: tested the corner of a turned square tile with long sides

why.hi: tile square hai, toh uska har kona right angle hai; ghumane se kona nahi badalta, aur 30 cm lambi bhuja se kona zyada nahi khulta, isliye tester bilkul fit hoga
why.en: the tile is a square, so each corner is a right angle; turning does not change a corner, and 30 cm long sides do not open it wider, so the tester fits exactly

simpler.hi: Do baatein ek-ek karke socho: tile ko ghumane se uska kona badla kya, aur lambi bhuja se kona zyada khula kya.
simpler.en: Think about two things one at a time: did turning the tile change its corner, and did the long sides open the corner wider.

leadIn.hi: Chalo, aaj ka ek aakhri sawaal, poore paath se.
leadIn.en: Okay, one last question for today, from the whole lesson.

leadIn.hi: Ab poore paath mein se bas ek sawaal aur aata hai.
leadIn.en: Now just one more question comes, from the whole lesson.

leadIn.hi: Jaane se pehle, aaj ki saari baaton par ek aakhri sawaal.
leadIn.en: Before we finish, one last question on everything from today.

viewCaption.hi: Board par wahi square tile do baar bani hai: pehli seedhi rakhi hai, aur doosri ghuma kar tirchi.
viewCaption.en: The board shows the same square tile twice: the first laid straight, and the second turned and slanting.

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki right angle kitaab ke kone jaisa hota hai, aur ghumane se kona nahi badalta. Phir angle ko uske khulne se naapa, aur circle aaya, jiska har point centre se barabar door hai.
covered.en: Today we saw that a right angle is like a book's corner, and that turning does not change a corner. Then we judged angles by their opening, and met the circle, all of it equally far from its centre.

goodbye.hi: Aaj ke liye itna hi, phir milte hain!
goodbye.en: That's all for today, see you next time!
